In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ionized gas in the central few hundred pc of the galaxy bulge, whether or not it is associated with an AGN, is a tracer of the hot gas and is supported against gravity by the same random motions as the stars.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ionized gas in the bulges of normal and AGN galaxies is dynamically supported by the stellar gravitational potential, and its origin is from stellar mass loss.
the dynamical properties of the ionized gas in the bulges of galaxies, whether or not they host AGNs, are consistent with those expected for a population of stars.
the ionized gas in galaxy bulges has an origin similar to that of stars and that its kinematics largely reflect the gravitational potential of the bulge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ionized gas in galaxy bulges is dynamically supported by the stellar gravitational field, and its kinematics are largely determined by stellar mass loss and the hot gas in galaxy halos.
ionized gas is not a dynamically dominant component of the inner regions of normal galaxies, but it is dynamically supported by the stellar bulge.
